newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebegue made BNP vice-chair, prepares euro.
newsitem.headline: Lebegue made BNP vice-chair, prepares euro.

text.p: BNP chairman Michel Pebereau said on Thursday managing director Daniel Lebegue would move to a post as vice-chairman in a management reorganisation following the retirement of current vice-chairman Jacques-Henri Wahl.
Jacques-Henri Wahl is retiring at the age of 65.

Baudoin Prot, Georges Chodron de Courcel and Vivien Levy Garboua become deputy managing directors, while keeping their operational duties, the former as head of French banking activity and the latter two in international operations.
Lebegue will be adviser to the chairman as well as chairman of various units and is also in charge of preparing BNP for the transition to the euro single currency.

Pebereau said the cost of the euro preparations was estimated at 1.6 billion francs, covering the necessary changes to information systems, training of staff and the creation of new commercial products linked to the euro.
He said BNP and partner Dresdner Bank AG would work very closely on euro products.
